sections.h2: Where to find the Cumberland County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
The office is in Room 114 of the Judge E. Maurice Braswell Cumberland County Courthouse, 117 Dick Street in Fayetteville. The land records line is 910-678-7775. Office hours and the yearly holiday schedule are posted at ccrod.org.

Land records reach back to 1754, which the office gives as the county's official start. The same counter handles notary oaths and vital records, and retired service members can file discharge papers (DD-214) free of charge.

sections.h2: Why filing time on a deed matters
sections.html:
A buyer in this state has no protection from rival claimants until the deed is on the public record at the courthouse. If two papers conflict, the one registered first generally prevails, which is why the recorded time stamp is worth checking.

These habits keep the paperwork clean:

  • Have each signature notarized before anything is carried to Dick Street.
  • Pair the deed with a payment covering the excise tax and the filing fee.
  • Ask the closing attorney what date and time the filing was stamped.
  • Save the book and page reference from the recorded copy.

Counter clerks cannot draft a deed or advise on its wording. That is attorney work.

The schedule on the office website dates from October 1, 2016. Filing an ordinary deed begins at $26.00 and a mortgage filing begins at $64.00. Other charges follow.

Recording fees at the Cumberland County office
Document or serviceFee
Deed or other instrument, first 15 pages$26.00, then $4.00 for each additional page
Mortgage or deed of trust, first 35 pages$64.00, then $4.00 for each additional page
Second instrument inside one document$10.00
Document in a non-standard format$25.00 added to the recording fee
SatisfactionsNo fee
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each page after
Plat or map recording$21.00 per page
DD-214 recordingNo fee

Pay by check or money order to the office. A document recorded a second time is charged as if new.

The rate is $2.00 per $1,000 of sale price, and a partial thousand is rounded up. The statute states the same rate as $1.00 per $500. It goes in with the filing fee and is written on page one of the deed.

The seller, whom the law calls the transferor, is the one who owes it, and the clerk collects before recording. Half goes to the county and half to the state. If the contract price is not a round number, your closing attorney can work out the amount.

sections.h2: What a deed needs before it is accepted
sections.html:
Page one has to name the preparer and carry a return address. The recording requirements page lists:

  • The draftsman line, usually written "Prepared by" or "Drawn by."
  • A return address block, also on page one.
  • The excise tax or revenue amount on the front of the deed.
  • Paper size, margins, type size and page count within state recording standards.
  • Signatures notarized before filing.

Satisfactions and UCC filings do not have to follow the formatting rules. A deed with the wrong layout is still taken, but $25.00 is added.

Enrollment is free, and an email arrives whenever a recorded document carries your name. The office pitches it as a guard against deed fraud. See a filing you never approved? Phone a real estate attorney.

To enroll, go to ccrod.org, pick Records Search, choose New Property Notification and follow the screens. An alert shows the matched name, the date, the book and page, and a link to the document. The alerts are no guarantee against fraud, but they help if you own a vacant or inherited Fayetteville property.

sections.h2: Deed records and the property tax listing
sections.html:
On January 1, Tax Administration looks to documents indexed here and in the Clerk of Court's estates division to decide who the listing owner is. The county keeps a permanent listing, so owners report only what changed, such as a deck, an in-ground pool or a remodel. Forms are due back by January 31.

Send them to Tax Administration, Attn: Real Estate Division, P.O. Box 449, Fayetteville, NC 28302, or drop them at Room 530 of the courthouse. Bills are due September 1. Interest of two percent starts January 6, with three-quarters of a percent more each month from February 1. For a sale partway through the year, ask Tax Administration who is billed.

An owner rated permanently and totally disabled through military service can apply at the assessor's office for a state exclusion of $45,000 in appraised value.

Cumberland County has 338,473 people, 146,623 housing units and 652.56 square miles of land. Owners occupy 55.0 percent of homes, which leaves a large rental market. Typical owner-occupied value is $199,200, typical gross rent is $1,222 a month and typical household income is $61,291. Individual streets vary.

If you are comparing sale options, remember that a typical sale here involves four recording-related pieces: the deed itself, the excise tax, the filing fee, and a satisfaction for any loan you pay off. Only the satisfaction is free, and the DD-214 recording is free for service members as well. Ask your attorney to list all four on the settlement statement so nothing is missed at closing. Questions about the amounts can go to the land records line at 910-678-7775.

sections.h2: What a seller should check before signing
sections.html:
Start with the loan. A satisfaction for a paid-off mortgage is recorded free, so a cleared loan should leave that document in the record. When payments have lapsed, the lender goes through a power-of-sale hearing before the clerk of superior court, and after the sale is reported anyone can file an upset bid within ten days, at least five percent over the price and $750.00 or more higher.

Then look at title: the last recorded deed, any liens, and whether a deed of trust is still open. If the house passed through an estate, the clerk's estates division has records worth reviewing. Your attorney usually runs this search, and your job is to hand over the old closing papers and any loan statements you have.

After closing, the executed deed is delivered here along with the tax and fee, and the stamped original returns to the address on page one. Selling for cash skips a lender's appraisal and underwriting, yet recording costs still apply. File the book and page numbers with your sale papers.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Cumberland County home sale?
faqs.a: The seller. The statute calls that person the transferor, and the tax is collected at the counter before the deed is recorded. The county's page shows $2.00 per $1,000 of price, and the statute shows $1.00 per $500.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Cumberland County?
faqs.a: Deeds begin at $26.00 for fifteen pages, plus $4.00 for each page beyond that. A mortgage begins at $64.00 for thirty-five pages. Satisfactions are free.

faqs.q: Can Register of Deeds staff draft my deed?
faqs.a: No. State law bars them from legal advice and from writing deeds. Get it drafted, signed and notarized first, and take wording questions to an attorney.

faqs.q: What is the Property Notification service?
faqs.a: A free email alert for when a document under your name is filed in Fayetteville. Enroll at ccrod.org under Records Search. The office calls it an early warning, not a fraud guarantee.

faqs.q: Where does a real property listing form go?
faqs.a: Mail it to Tax Administration, Attn: Real Estate Division, P.O. Box 449, Fayetteville, NC 28302, or hand it in at Room 530 of the courthouse. January 31 is the due date, so changes count that year.
